questions.question: How do scientists calculate the average global surface temperature?
options: By taking measurements from a single central weather station in each country
By calculating it from tens of thousands of measurements worldwide
By estimating it based on satellite images of cloud cover alone
By averaging temperatures from only the hottest and coldest places on Earth

questions.question: When monitoring climate change, what are regional temperatures compared with to identify anomalies?
options: The long-term average temperature for that specific region
The temperature of the closest ocean at that time
The global average temperature of the equator
The highest temperature ever recorded in that country

questions.question: What has been the general trend in overall global surface temperatures since the industrial revolution in the 1850s?
options: Temperatures have remained completely stable
Temperatures have been steadily decreasing
Temperatures have been increasing
Temperatures have fluctuated with no overall trend

questions.question: Which of the following provides scientists with evidence of longer-term historical temperature changes before modern records began?
options: Historical weather diaries and ship logs only
Deep ocean sand dunes and volcanic ash layers
Satellite data from ancient orbits
Evidence from tree rings and ice cores

questions.question: How do scientists explain the contribution of increased levels of greenhouse gases to global warming?
options: They trap more of the heat emitted from the Earth's surface
They reflect more solar radiation back into space before it reaches Earth
They increase the rate of nuclear fusion inside the Sun
They create holes in the atmosphere that let more direct sunlight in

questions.question: What is the main environmental consequence of increasing levels of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere?
options: A gradual decrease in global sea levels
Global warming and climate change
A decrease in the rate of photosynthesis worldwide
The cooling of the Earth's core

questions.question: How does the potency of methane as a greenhouse gas compare to that of carbon dioxide?
options: Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide
Carbon dioxide is much more potent than methane
Both gases have exactly the same potency
Methane has no greenhouse effect compared to carbon dioxide

questions.question: What is the primary effect of greenhouse gases naturally present in the atmosphere?
options: They keep the atmosphere warmer than it would be without them
They prevent any heat from the Sun from reaching Earth's surface
They cause the Earth's atmosphere to slowly drift into space
They cool the atmosphere to prevent overheating

questions.question: What primary source of heating controls the average temperature of Earth?
options: Geothermal energy from the Earth's core
Heating from the Sun
Friction from tectonic plate movements
Heat released from burning fossil fuels

questions.question: How does the melting of land-based ice sheets due to increased temperatures affect oceans?
options: It has no effect because ice sheets float on the ocean already
It cools the oceans down, causing the sea levels to drop
It moves more water into the sea, causing sea levels to rise
It increases the salt concentration of the oceans

questions.question: Why does the melting of sea ice in summer not raise global sea levels?
options: The water from sea ice evaporates immediately into space
Sea ice is already floating in the water, so melting it does not add water to the sea
Sea ice is made of fresh water which takes up less space when it melts
The ocean floor sinks to accommodate the melted sea ice

questions.question: Besides melting ice sheets, what is another major cause of rising sea levels as global temperatures increase?
options: Warmer oceans and seas expand, causing sea levels to rise
Undersea volcanic eruptions increase in size
Increased rainfall directly fills the ocean basins
Earth's gravity pulls more water from the atmosphere

questions.question: How do electric vehicles compare to petrol and diesel vehicles regarding fuel use?
options: Electric vehicles burn fuel directly, while petrol cars do not
Electric vehicles do not burn fuels, but fuels may be burned to generate electricity
Electric vehicles require more diesel to run their internal generators
Both types of vehicles burn exactly the same amount of petrol

questions.question: What is the process of carbon capture and storage (CCS)?
options: It separates CO₂ from other emissions and stores it in suitable deep underground locations
It absorbs CO₂ into giant water tanks located in city centres
It converts CO₂ into oxygen using large artificial forests
It traps CO₂ in the upper atmosphere using specialized satellites

questions.question: What is a major disadvantage of using carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology?
options: It increases the amount of CO₂ released into the atmosphere
It only works during the night when temperatures are low
It can reduce CO₂ emissions but is very expensive
It can only store CO₂ for a few days before it leaks

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of global greenhouse gas emissions is produced by the energy sector?
options: Around 10%
Around 25%
Around 50%
Around 75%

questions.question: Under what conditions does a car use more energy to travel a distance of 100 km?
options: If it is lighter and travels at lower speeds
If it is heavier or travels at higher speeds
If it travels on a completely flat, straight road
If its windows are closed and it travels slowly

questions.question: How does maintaining the correct air pressure in car tyres affect energy use?
options: Cars use less energy if their tyres are inflated to the correct pressure
Cars use more energy because correct pressure increases friction
Tyre pressure has no effect on a car's energy consumption
Correctly inflated tyres only save energy when driving backwards

questions.question: Why will renewable energy resources not run out?
options: They are stored in massive, infinite tanks underground
They are replenished more quickly than we use them up
Humans have agreed to use them only once a year
They are created by burning fossil fuels

questions.question: Which technology produces electricity directly without needing an electric generator?
options: Wind turbines
Hydroelectric dams
Coal-fired power stations
Solar panels
